Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the UniBank Financial Group Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. As a reminder, ladies and gentlemen, this conference is being recorded. I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson:
Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to review UniBank Financial Group's results for the Q3 2024. With me this morning are Johnathan Reyes, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Risk Officer; David Kim, Chief Credit Officer; Elena Vasquez, Chief Technology Officer; and Robert Hale, Chief Operating Officer.

Before we begin, let me remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of these factors.

I will now turn the call over to Johnathan Reyes.

Johnathan Reyes:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. UniBank Financial Group delivered exceptional results in the Q3 2024, exceeding expectations and demonstrating the strength of our diversified business model.

Our key priorities for this year remain focused on:
1. Accelerating revenue growth
2. Improving profitability
3. Managing risk effectively
4. Investing in technology and innovation
5. Enhancing customer experience
6. Strengthening our brand
7. Delivering value to our shareholders.

Now, I'd like to provide some highlights on key areas. On technology investments and their impact on efficiency, we've committed around $750 million over the past two years, driving our cost-to-income ratio down 720 basis points to 56.2% through cloud migrations, AI tools, and RPA. Regarding operating expenses trends and key drivers, non-interest expenses rose modestly 6% year-over-year to $2.52 billion, with our efficiency ratio at 57.8%, reflecting investments balanced by productivity gains. Our key strategic initiatives have progressed well, with digital platform Nexus boosting user adoption 28% and APAC loan growth at 22%. On asset sensitivity and interest rate risk management, we maintain a positive $70 billion gap, positioning us for NII upside from rate stability. Deposit growth and mix show total deposits up 7.2% to $285 billion, with core transactional and savings holding strong at 75%. Cost of deposits averaged 2.42%, managed tightly amid competition through pricing discipline. Finally, our guidance assumptions include moderate GDP growth, three Fed cuts, and NII expansion to 3.25-3.35%.

I will now turn the call over to Michael Chen to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Michael Chen:
Thank you, Johnathan, and good morning. UniBank Financial Group reported net income of $850 million for the Q3 2024, or $2.10 per share. Our results reflect strong revenue growth, disciplined expense management, and a healthy credit environment.

Net interest income increased 8% driven by higher loan yields and deposit growth. Non-interest income was up 12%, reflecting strong performance in trading and fees. Our capital ratios remain strong, with CET1 at 12.8%, and we are well-positioned to support future growth.

Let me expand on these results with more granularity, starting with our technology investments and their profound effects on efficiency. In a competitive landscape pressured by fintechs like Stripe, Adyen, Chime, and Revolut, we've strategically allocated about $750 million—or 12% of total OpEx—over the last 24 months to tech, generating strong returns via cost savings and revenue uplift. Investments break down to 40% in cloud infrastructure, 25% in AI/ML, 20% in RPA/STP, and the rest in cybersecurity, data platforms, and open banking APIs. This effort improved our CIR by 720 bps to 56.2%, below the industry 62% average per McKinsey, and non-interest expenses as a share of assets to 1.85% from 2.1%.

Our cloud shift to AWS/Azure hybrid cut TCO 28%, reducing mainframe spend from 35% to under 10% of IT, handling 15% higher payment volumes via RTP and FedNow. AI tools on TensorFlow/Snowflake slashed fraud false positives 45% to 12 bps of deposits, below peer medians; chatbots managed 68% of inquiries, lifting NPS 14 points and cutting call center staff 22%; lending AI with Plaid/Experian data sped approvals to 4 days, boosting originations 18%. RPA via UiPath/Automation Anywhere automated 42% of reconciliations and KYC/AML, shortening wire settlements 35% and freeing 1,200 FTEs, for $220 million run-rate savings and 3.2x ROI.

By region, North America (55% revenue) saw U.S. CIR at 54% with embedded finance APIs for Shopify/Affirm; Europe (25%) gained 30% compliance efficiency via RegTech and Hyperledger despite PSD3/DORA costs; APAC (18%) achieved 52% retail efficiency via WeChat/Alipay. These build moats, growing non-interest revenue 14% via APIs/data services, targeting 50% CIR by 2026 with $400 million more in quantum crypto, edge computing, and deposit analytics as costs rose 45 bps.

Next, operating expenses, reported as non-interest expense, totaled $2.52 billion in Q3, up 6% YoY from $2.38 billion but flat QoQ, or 5% adjusted excluding $45 million FDIC assessment. Efficiency ratio hit 57.8%, down 220 bps YoY, best Q3 in five years; nine-month total $7.41 billion, up 7%. Compensation/benefits at 42% or $1.06 billion rose 8% on 4% salaries and 12% variable pay amid talent competition with Goldman and Stripe, FTEs up 1.2% to 48,500 in digital/risk. Occupancy/equipment up 3% to $285 million on leases, offset by 15% branch closures to 1,200, with app handling 78% transactions like JPM.

Tech/data processing up 12% to $520 million on cloud amortization (65% complete, mainframes down 18%) and genAI for fraud/wealth via UniWealth, lifting detection 25%. Professional fees up 9% to $310 million on reg projects like LIBOR/Dodd-Frank; compliance up 10% to $180 million on SEC climate/EU DORA. Other up 4% to $165 million on marketing for savings products. North America OpEx up 4% (55% base), EMEA 10% (25%), APAC 15% (15% post-DBS), LatAm stable. 'Efficiency 2.0' targets mid-single-digit 2024 growth via RPA ($120M savings), outsourcing to BNY; jaw closed with revenue +300 bps faster. FY guide $10.0-10.2B, low-57s efficiency.

Turning to deposit growth and mix, our franchise grew total deposits 7.2% YoY to $285 billion, +1.5% QoQ or $4.2 billion, beating FDIC 1.1% average. LDR at 82%, below peers. Transactional (DDAs/NOW) $114 billion or 40%, up 4.1% YoY, non-interest DDAs $63B (22%, beta 15 bps). Savings/MMDAs $100B (35%), up 12.3% YoY/+3.2% QoQ at 3.85% average (beta 65%). Time deposits $71B (25%), up 18.6% YoY, brokered 15% via IntraFi, retail via app. Shift to time/savings (time +4 pts share), but core 75% > peers; post-SVB inflows $2.8B. U.S. +8.5%, Europe +9%, APAC +14%. Strategies: AI app personalization, Plaid ACH, Round-Up ($450M), bundles, pricing via RateWatch, risk monitoring. NIM +25 bps to 3.55%, guide 6-8% FY growth.

On cost of deposits, average at 2.42% up 125 bps YoY/+8 bps QoQ, beta 38% < peer 45%. Non-interest 32% ($28.2B), interest-bearing 68% ($59.8B) at 3.56%. Savings/MMDAs (42%) 3.12% +140 bps, Priority Plus to 4.10%; CDs (18%) 4.28%, promo 4.50%. Southeast costs 3.05%, Midwest 2.15%. Pressures from SoFi/Chime 4.5-5%, MMFs 5.20%, JPM tiers. Organic 92% core, +4.2% YoY > industry. Pillars: AI pricing (Salesforce), YieldGuard ($650M), regional builds. Q2 costs 2.55-2.60%, FY 2.70%, NIM -15 bps offset.

Our key strategic initiatives show strong progress across digital transformation, geographic expansion, and sustainability. Nexus platform grew digital users 28% to 18.2M (72% base), volumes $450B, mobile deposits 65%; AI fraud cut losses $250M, false positives 42%; embedded BNPL UniFlex +60% merchants, $180M fees. APAC loans +22% to $45B, deposits +30% $32B (18% NII); Europe deposits +15% €28B, green mortgages €4.2B; U.S. core deposits +12% $420B, LDR 78%. Sustainability: $6.5B green bonds, $120B portfolio (22%). Digital ROTE 14.2%, CIR 52%, NPS 68. Q4 targets 20% digital rev, $10B sustainable, APAC 22% NII.

Regarding asset sensitivity and IRR management, post-Fed cut to 5.25%, NII record $2.8B +8% YoY, NIM 3.65% stable. Asset-sensitive: NII beta 0.45/+100 bps ($250-300M), gap +$70B (6.5% assets): 0-3m +$25B (SOFR C&I), 3-12m +$45B (ARMs 35% mortgages), 1-5y -$10B. Deposit beta 65%, DDA 42%. Stress: +200 bps NII +4.2%, -100 bps -2.1%, within limits. U.S. SOFR dominant, Europe hedged, APAC premium. Tools: Moody's AXIS modeling, $40B swaps (pay-fixed 3.85%), DV01 -$12M. FlexRate ARMs, tiered CDs. Guide NII peak $11.5B FY.

Finally, key guidance assumptions: U.S. GDP 2.3% 2024/1.8-2.0% 2025, unemployment 4.1-4.3%, PCE 2.2%. NII +5-7%, NIM 3.25-3.35% (3x25bps cuts), loans +4-6%; fees +8-10%, AUM $450B. Provisions $1.2-1.3B, NCOs 45-55 bps, NPLs 95-105 bps. Expenses $8.8-9.0B, 56-58% efficiency. U.S. 4% deposits, Europe fees +10%, APAC high-single. CET1 11.5-12%, buybacks $2.5B, dividend +45-50 bps.

Lisa Patel:
Thank you, Michael. From a risk management perspective, we are closely monitoring interest rate fluctuations, commercial real estate exposures, and geopolitical tensions. We are taking proactive steps to mitigate these risks and maintain a strong risk profile, leveraging our robust ALM framework and stress testing as outlined.

David Kim:
Good morning. Our credit quality remains exceptionally strong with non-performing loans at 0.85% and net charge-offs at 0.42%. We are actively managing our loan portfolio and remain confident in our ability to navigate the current economic environment. Specifically, the performance of our commercial and industrial loan portfolio has been strong, with low delinquencies supported by diversified sectors.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you. I'd like to provide an update on our technology initiatives. We are making significant progress on our digital transformation, including the launch of UniBank Nexus which has seen 28% adoption growth in terms of customer uptake and substantial efficiency gains across operations.

Robert Hale:
Good morning. We are focused on operational excellence and driving efficiency across the organization. Key initiatives include robotic process automation for back-office workflows and cloud modernization, which are contributing to improved productivity and $220 million in run-rate cost savings.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, at this time we will open the line for questions. [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from Mike Rossi with Keefe, Bruyette & Woods. Please go ahead.

Mike Rossi:
Good morning. Can you provide further insights into your technology investments and their impact on efficiency?

Johnathan Reyes:
Thanks, Mike. As Michael detailed, our $750 million tech spend has been transformative, with cloud cutting TCO 28%, AI reducing fraud losses significantly, and RPA delivering 3.2x ROI. Regionally, it's lowered CIR most in North America and APAC, positioning us for 50% target by 2026 while growing non-interest fees.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Susan Lee with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Susan Lee:
What are your plans for operating expenses going forward?

Michael Chen:
Good question, Susan. We're guiding $10.0-10.2 billion full-year adjusted, 6-7% growth, with Q4 seasonal comp and tech rollouts. Discipline via RPA, zero-based budgeting, and outsourcing keeps efficiency in low-57s, supporting 12%+ ROTE amid macro uncertainty.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Wong with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

David Wong:
How are you managing asset sensitivity and interest rate risks?

Lisa Patel:
Thanks, David. Our positive 6.5% gap and 0.45 beta provide NII upside, hedged with $40 billion swaps and advanced modeling. We've stress-tested cuts and shocks, staying within limits, and products like FlexRate ensure stability as the Fed eases.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Carter with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter:
Can you discuss the performance of your deposit portfolio?

David Kim:
Absolutely, Emily. Deposits grew 7.2% to $285 billion, core mix 75%, costs controlled at 2.42% with betas 38%. Strategies like AI personalization and regional focus have retained stickiness, funding loan growth internally and supporting NIM.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the conference back over to Johnathan Reyes for any closing remarks.

Johnathan Reyes:
Thank you for your interest in UniBank Financial Group. We appreciate you joining us today. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
